transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vekulman.
President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin have
concluded their trilateral meeting today in Shenzhen, China.
Trump asked the other two leaders to bear in mind the responsibility their countries
have to decrease the number of nuclear weapons in the world.
Russia's Deepa Shivarom reports on the historic meeting of the three leaders the first time
they've all met together.
Trump said the U.S., China, and Russia were "uniquely positioned to discuss denuclearization,"
a topic he wanted to talk about in the meeting, but China is hesitant to engage in.
Trump even acknowledged it was hard to act on.
I must say it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do because once you have the nuclear
weapons it's very hard to not have them.
It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country.
Trump also said that three countries have to maintain "open, respectful, and productive
dialogue."
And he emphasized a key part of his own stance on global leadership, saying that it's not
beneficial for leaders to avoid speaking with each other even when they have disagreements.
Deepa Shivarom, NPR News, Shenzhen.
Ukrainian forces hit the Crimean Bridge again earlier this week.
Another Ukrainian strike collapsed an entire bridge section.
It links the Crimean Peninsula to Russia.
Others say the attack may have been timed to humiliate Russian President Vladimir Putin
ahead of his trilateral meeting with Presidents Trump and Xi.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley has more.
Ukraine says it was a carefully planned, seven-phase operation which was carried out over multiple
weeks and first included the weakening of Russian air defenses around one of its most
heavily guarded infrastructure sites.
It means a lot for Ukraine because for Putin, the Korean Bridge or Crimean Bridge is also
known is a huge symbol of his propaganda.
That's Ukrainian Parliament member Alexander Merezhko.
He says the successful bridge attack is a humiliation for Putin on the world stage and
has boosted Ukrainian's morale as they come under relentless Russian drone and missile
attack ahead of their fifth winter at war.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
The artificial intelligence company, Anthropic, says it has put nearly one billion shares
on the market.
The price is $83 per share.
NPR's John Ruich reports on the record-breaking initial public offering.
Just five years old, Anthropic is a powerhouse of the AI world with a clawed family of models.
Its IPO had been widely anticipated and brings in over $81.3 billion.
That exceeds the $75 billion that Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in its IPO earlier this year.
Anthropic's listing had strong demand despite coming at a time of growing concern about
a possible AI bubble.
Its shares will start trading on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol A-N-T, and Anthropic
is a financial supporter of NPR.
John Ruich, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The UN's highest court in The Hague is reading out its decision on whether the military junta
of Myanmar committed genocide against Thuringia Muslims.
The International Court of Justice has determined the Myanmar junta killed some 10,000 Rohingyas
in its 2017 military operations.
And crucially, the justices have ruled that Myanmar, quote, "committed acts that violated
parts of the genocide convention."
Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fled in the midst of rapes, the murders of children,
and widespread arson attacks.
In the U.S., a new survey finds that more than four in 10 adults say they've had at
least one serious financial hardship over the past year.
NPR's Jennifer Luden reports that's the highest level in a decade.
The most common hardships?
Having to borrow money from family or friends to pay bills and not paying an important bill
in full.
That's according to the American Family Survey by researchers at Brigham Young University.
The poll also reported being hungry, forgoing medical care, having to move in with someone
else, or losing housing altogether.
The poll also finds broad concern about being able to afford a home or family.
In fact, when younger adults were asked what's the most important thing to do before having
a child, being financially stable topped the list.
Looking ahead, most Americans of all ages say the biggest threat to their finances is
inflation.
Jennifer Luden, NPR News.
On Wall Street, in pre-market trading, stock futures are significantly higher.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump, Xi, and Putin conclude trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, urging nuclear weapons reduction
Ukrainian forces strike and collapse a section of the Crimean Bridge linking Crimea to Russia
Anthropic launches IPO of nearly one billion shares at $83 each, raising over $81 billion
UN top court rules Myanmar's military junta committed acts violating genocide convention against Rohingya
Survey finds over four in 10 US adults faced serious financial hardship, highest level in a decade
Stock futures significantly higher in pre-market trading on Wall Street
